newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HOCKEY-ANOTHER TOURNAMENT SUCCESS FOR NETHERLANDS.
newsitem.headline: HOCKEY-ANOTHER TOURNAMENT SUCCESS FOR NETHERLANDS.

text.p: The Netherlands beat World Cup holders Pakistan 4-0 on Sunday to win their third hockey tournament out of four since being crowned Olympic champions at Atlanta last year.
The home side won all their three games and scored 14 goals in the four-nation tournament which moved to its third venue, the Wagener Stadium at Amstelveen, for its final day.
The proficiency of Bram Lomans, the Dutch corner specialist, undid a Pakistan side that dominated early play.
Lomans scored from successive corners in the middle of the second half to put his side 3-0 ahead. He finished the tournament as leading scorer with seven goals.
The other Dutch goals came from Remco van Wijk in the 27th minute after an excellent Dutch combination and from a solo effort by captain Stephan Veen.

The Dutch have had the edge over Pakistan since they lost to them on strokes in the 1994 World Cup final. Sunday's win was their fifth in their last six meetings and they were one goal short of equalling their biggest-ever victory margin over the Pakistanis.
England, who beat Pakistan and lost to the Netherlands earlier in the tournament, finished second despite being held to a 2-2 draw by South Africa in their final game.
Greg Nicol, joint top scorer at the Atlanta Olympics, scored 23 seconds from time to give South Africa their only point of the tournament.
